    ENGLISH

    Recent methods for injecting graph structure into LLM prompts include graph soft prompting, in which a graph neural network (GNN) learns graph-specific tokens that capture relational information among entities in textual prompts. G-Retriever combines graph soft prompts with a verbalized description of the same graph to strengthen the textual prompt signal. We conduct an in-depth analysis of G-Retriever and uncover a pathological behavior we term token collapse. Across three benchmarks, three graph encoders, two LLM families, and both frozen and LoRA-adapted models, G-Retriever's graph tokens become almost indistinguishable across inputs. We provide evidence that the same failure is inherited by subsequent methods, even with multi-token pooling. Under the standard setup, swapping a token with the dataset mean, a token from another example, or one derived from a corrupted graph produces no resolved answer-level effect in accuracy. Moreover, a learned constant prompt that never accesses the graph matches or surpasses G-Retriever on all three benchmarks. These findings indicate that, rather than conveying graph content as intended, the collapsed token functions primarily as a generic soft prompt. We also examine conditions linked to this collapse and propose a two-stage procedure that yields non-collapsed tokens while maintaining competitive performance in most cases. However, token variability alone does not prove that the model uses graph information: via interventions and decoding probes, we show that depending on the configuration, a token can reflect the question, an answer prior, or graph-derived content that the LLM may or may not use. Overall, our results offer a practical approach to evaluating graph-token alignment rather than inferring it from task accuracy alone. Code to reproduce our experiments is available at https://github.com/difra100/Token_Collapse_KGQA.

    将图结构注入 LLM 提示词的近期方法包括图软提示，其中图神经网络（GNN）学习特定于图的词元，以捕捉文本提示中实体之间的关系信息。G-Retriever 将图软提示与同一图的文字描述相结合，以增强文本提示信号。我们对 G-Retriever 进行了深入分析，发现了一种我们称为词元坍缩的病态行为。在三个基准、三种图编码器、两个 LLM 系列以及冻结和 LoRA 适配模型上，G-Retriever 的图词元在不同输入之间变得几乎无法区分。我们提供证据表明，后续方法也继承了同样的失效，即使采用多词元池化也如此。在标准设置下，将一个词元替换为数据集均值、另一个示例中的词元或由受损图生成的词元，都不会对答案层面的准确率产生可分辨的影响。此外，一个从不访问图的学习得到的常量提示，在全部三个基准上的表现都能与 G-Retriever 持平或超越它。这些发现表明，坍缩后的词元并未如预期传达图内容，而主要充当通用软提示。我们还考察了与这种坍缩相关的条件，并提出一种两阶段流程，可生成未坍缩的词元，同时在大多数情况下保持有竞争力的性能。然而，仅有词元变化性并不能证明模型使用了图信息：通过干预和解码探测，我们表明，视具体配置而定，词元可能反映问题、答案先验，或图衍生内容，而 LLM 可能会也可能不会使用这些内容。总体而言，我们的结果提供了一种实用方法，用于评估图词元对齐，而不是仅凭任务准确率推断对齐情况。复现我们实验的代码见 https://github.com/difra100/Token_Collapse_KGQA。

    Hayden Prairie, Jacob M. Ryan, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, and Daniel Y. Fu

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper proposes a training method that makes recurrent representations converge across loop iterations, enabling KV-cache sharing while preserving model quality and reducing inference costs. This gives substantial mechanistic insight into representation dynamics and a core systems contribution to memory-efficient inference; composing KV-sharing with other compression methods is secondary to that focus.

    本文提出一种训练方法，使循环表征在不同循环迭代间趋于收敛，从而在保持模型质量的同时实现 KV 缓存共享并降低推理成本。这既深入揭示了表征动力学机制，也为内存高效推理带来了核心系统贡献；将 KV 共享与其他压缩方法结合是次要内容。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Looped architectures scale quality while keeping parameter count fixed by repeatedly passing activations through the same block of layers. During inference, each recurrence generates independent KV-caches, causing memory to grow linearly. To address this challenge, prior work has proposed KV-sharing (i.e., sharing KV-caches across depth), finding that, in some cases, the KV-cache of the final recurrence can be shared with the earlier recurrences without quality loss, a property we denote as KV-shareability. However, the mechanisms underlying KV-shareability remain poorly understood, with even identically trained looped architectures not consistently exhibiting it. In this paper, we study how KV-shareability can be enabled in looped models. We propose a two-stage method: in the first stage, we use stochastic depth during pretraining, which induces contractive residual dynamics that drive representations toward a common limit across recurrences. In the second stage, we propose BeNice!, a post-training method that broadcasts the final recurrence's KV-cache into the first recurrence, training it to produce compatible residuals while preserving the original model's quality. As a result, BeNice! enables KV-shareability while matching standard finetuning's unshared validation perplexity. Using BeNice!, we show that KV-sharing is complementary to alternative KV-compression methods, composing with memory-efficient sequence mixers (e.g., multi-latent attention, Kimi delta attention) and low-precision KV-cache quantization (e.g., fp8, mxfp8, nvfp4). Finally, in simulated low-memory, long-context inference, KV-sharing improves cache hit rates by up to 31.4%, increases throughput by up to 23.6%, and reduces p90 time-to-first-token by up to 83.6%.

    中文

    循环架构通过反复将激活传过同一层块，在固定参数量的同时提升质量。在推理期间，每次循环都会生成独立的 KV 缓存，导致内存随循环次数线性增长。为应对这一挑战，先前工作提出了 KV 共享（即跨深度共享 KV 缓存），并发现有时可以将最后一次循环的 KV 缓存与较早循环共享而不损失质量；我们将这一特性称为 KV 可共享性。然而，人们对 KV 可共享性背后的机制仍知之甚少，甚至经过相同训练的循环架构也不一定能稳定表现出这一特性。本文研究如何在循环模型中实现 KV 可共享性。我们提出一种两阶段方法：第一阶段在预训练期间使用随机深度，由此产生收缩残差动力学，推动不同循环中的表征趋向共同极限。第二阶段，我们提出 BeNice！，一种后训练方法，将最后一次循环的 KV 缓存广播至第一次循环，并训练其产生兼容的残差，同时保持原模型质量。因此，BeNice！实现了 KV 可共享性，同时使未共享缓存时的验证困惑度达到标准微调方法的水平。借助 BeNice！，我们表明 KV 共享与其他 KV 压缩方法互为补充，可与高内存效率的序列混合器（例如多潜变量注意力、Kimi delta attention）以及低精度 KV 缓存量化（例如 fp8、mxfp8、nvfp4）结合。最后，在模拟的低内存、长上下文推理中，KV 共享将缓存命中率最高提升 31.4%，吞吐量最高提升 23.6%，并将第 90 百分位的首词元生成时间最多降低 83.6%。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting elicits step-by-step rationales that appear to explain model predictions, but there is no guarantee these steps causally drive the final answer. In standard autoregressive generation, dense attention allows each reasoning step to attend to the full context, enabling the model to derive answers through direct lookup while generating plausible-sounding but post-hoc justifications. We introduce CausalCoT, an inference framework that enforces causal transparency by decomposing problems into a directed acyclic graph of atomic sub-questions, evaluating each node in an isolated context containing only its direct causal parents. This Markovian structure removes attention pathways to non-parent content, making downstream predictions sensitive to local reasoning rather than global context leakage. Across a diverse suite of reasoning benchmarks, CausalCoT preserves competitive predictive performance while improving explanation faithfulness, increasing causal sensitivity of intermediate reasoning steps by an average of 12 and up to 21 percentage points over the strongest baseline. The structured dependency graph additionally enables test-time interventions in which local corrections propagate predictably through downstream reasoning.

    While ML model training and inference are both GPU-intensive, CPU-based data processing is often the bottleneck. Existing distributed data processing systems assume homogeneous resource requirements. They excel at CPU-based computation but either under-utilize heterogeneous resources or impose high overheads on failure and reconfiguration. We introduce Ray Data, a scalable system for heterogeneous workloads spanning batch inference and ML training. The key idea is to combine dynamic task creation for memory efficiency with dynamic task placement for operator elasticity. Making both decisions dynamically allows the system to adapt to heterogeneous pipelines where the memory and compute requirements per operator are unknown and variable over time. Ray Data addresses two challenges: (1) leveraging dynamic task creation for memory-efficient pipelining, and (2) designing a task placement policy that jointly allocates heterogeneous compute and memory resources to maximize throughput while limiting memory usage. Ray Data improves throughput on heterogeneous batch inference pipelines by 2.6-12$\times$ compared to traditional data processing systems.     Large language model (LLM) agents have shown impressive reasoning capabilities in interactive decision-making tasks. These agents interact with environment through intermediate interfaces, such as predefined action spaces and interaction rules, which mediate the perception and action. However, mismatches often happen between the internal expectations of the agent regarding the influence of its issued actions and the actual state transitions in the environment, a phenomenon referred to as agent-environment misalignment. While prior work has invested substantially in improving agent strategies and environment design, the critical role of the interface still remains underexplored. In this work, we empirically demonstrate that agent-environment misalignment poses a significant bottleneck to agent performance. To mitigate this issue, we propose ALIGN, an Auto-Aligned Interface Generation framework that alleviates the misalignment by enriching the interface. Specifically, the ALIGN-generated interface enhances both the static information of the environment and the step-wise observations returned to the agent. Implemented as a lightweight wrapper, this interface achieves the alignment without modifying either the agent logic or the environment code. Experiments across multiple domains including embodied tasks, web navigation and tool-use, show consistent performance improvements, with up to a 45.67% success rate improvement observed in ALFWorld. Meanwhile, ALIGN-generated interface can generalize across different agent architectures and LLM backbones without interface regeneration. Code and experimental results are available at https://github.com/THUNLP-MT/ALIGN.

    Accurate univariate forecasting remains a pressing need in real-world systems, such as energy markets, hydrology, retail demand, and IoT monitoring, where signals are often intermittent and horizons span both short- and long-term. While transformers and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures are increasingly favored for time-series forecasting, a key gap persists: MoE models typically require complicated training with both the main forecasting loss and auxiliary load-balancing losses, along with careful routing/temperature tuning, which hinders practical adoption. In this paper, we propose a model architecture that simplifies the training process for univariate time series forecasting and effectively addresses both long- and short-term horizons, including intermittent patterns. Our approach combines sparse MoE computation with a novel attention-inspired gating mechanism that replaces the traditional one-layer softmax router. Through extensive empirical evaluation, we demonstrate that our gating design naturally promotes balanced expert utilization and achieves superior predictive accuracy without requiring the auxiliary load-balancing losses typically used in classical MoE implementations. The model achieves better performance while utilizing only a fraction of the parameters required by state-of-the-art transformer models, such as PatchTST. Furthermore, experiments across diverse datasets confirm that our MoE architecture with the proposed gating mechanism is more computationally efficient than LSTM for both long- and short-term forecasting, enabling cost-effective inference. These results highlight the potential of our approach for practical time-series forecasting applications where both accuracy and computational efficiency are critical.

MENTOR performs metacognitive self-assessment, using strategies such as perspective-taking and consequential reasoning to uncover latent model misalignments.     Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in situations where human values are at stake, such as decision-making tasks that involve reasoning when performed by humans. We investigate the so-called reasoning capabilities of LLMs over novel symbolic representations by introducing an experimental framework that tests their ability to process and manipulate unfamiliar symbols. We introduce semantic deceptions: situations in which symbols carry misleading semantic associations due to their form, such as being embedded in specific contexts, designed to probe whether LLMs can maintain symbolic abstraction or whether they default to exploiting learned semantic associations. We redefine standard digits and mathematical operators using novel symbols, and task LLMs with solving simple calculations expressed in this altered notation. The objective is: (1) to assess LLMs' capacity for abstraction and manipulation of arbitrary symbol systems; (2) to evaluate their ability to resist misleading semantic cues that conflict with the task's symbolic logic. Through experiments with four LLMs we show that semantic cues can significantly deteriorate reasoning models' performance on very simple tasks. They reveal limitations in current LLMs' ability for symbolic manipulations and highlight a tendency to over-rely on surface-level semantics, suggesting that chain-of-thoughts may amplify reliance on statistical correlations. Even in situations where LLMs seem to correctly follow instructions, semantic cues still impact basic capabilities. These limitations raise ethical and societal concerns, undermining the widespread and pernicious tendency to attribute reasoning abilities to LLMs and suggesting how LLMs might fail, in particular in decision-making contexts where robust symbolic reasoning is essential and should not be compromised by residual semantic associations inherited from the model's training.

We investigate the Imperfective Paradox, a logical phenomenon where the past progressive aspect entails event realization for activities (e.g., running $\to$ ran) but not for accomplishments (e.g., building $\nrightarrow$ built). We introduce ImperfectiveNLI, a diagnostic dataset designed to probe this distinction across diverse semantic classes. Evaluating state-of-the-art open-weight models, we uncover a pervasive Teleological Bias: models systematically hallucinate completion for goal-oriented events, even overriding explicit textual cancellation. Prompting interventions partially reduce this bias but trigger a calibration crisis, causing models to incorrectly reject valid entailments for atelic verbs. Representational analyses further show that while internal embeddings often distinguish progressive from simple past forms, inference decisions are dominated by strong priors about goal attainment. Taken together, our findings indicate that these current open-weight LLMs operate as predictive narrative engines rather than faithful logical reasoners, and that resolving aspectual inference requires moving beyond prompting toward structurally grounded alignment.

    ENGLISH

    Self-training systems often degenerate due to the lack of an external criterion for judging data quality, leading to reward hacking and semantic drift. This paper provides a proof-of-concept system architecture for stable self-training under sparse external feedback and bounded memory, and empirically characterises its learning dynamics and failure modes. We introduce a self-training architecture in which learning is mediated exclusively by environmental viability, rather than by reward, objective functions, or externally defined fitness criteria. Candidate behaviours are executed under real resource constraints, and only those whose environmental effects both persist and preserve the possibility of future interaction are propagated. The environment does not provide semantic feedback, dense rewards, or task-specific supervision; selection operates solely through differential survival of behaviours as world-altering events, making proxy optimisation impossible and rendering reward-hacking evolutionarily unstable. Analysis of semantic dynamics shows that improvement arises primarily through the persistence of effective and repeatable strategies under a regime of consolidation and pruning, a paradigm we refer to as negative-space learning (NSL), and that models develop meta-learning strategies (such as deliberate experimental failure in order to elicit informative error messages) without explicit instruction. This work establishes that environment-grounded selection enables sustainable open-ended self-improvement, offering a viable path toward more robust and generalisable autonomous systems without reliance on human-curated data or complex reward shaping.

    SpatialMem is a memory-based system which integrates 3D geometry, semantics, and language with one another in one combined, queryable representation. Starting with casually recorded egocentric RGB video, SpatialMem recreates metrically scaled interior scenes, recognizes structural 3D anchors (walls, doors, windows) as the first-layer scaffold, and associates open-vocabulary object nodes with evidence patches, visual embeddings, and two-layer descriptions to 3D coordinates, enabling spatial-relation reasoning, language-directed retrieval, and QA without special sensors. We test at scale on public benchmarks. On VSI-Bench ($288$ videos, $5{,}130$ questions) SpatialMem scores $37.5$ overall with RGB alone, and its margin is precisely where a metric memory should earn it (room size $41.4$ vs.\ $24.4$ with a same-size frame model). On the episodic-memory task of OpenEQA ($953$ questions) the memory serialised to text is lower than the blind control, but as evidence-frame retrieval it recovers frame-level accuracy, matching uniform sampling at an equal eight-frame budget and pulling ahead as the budget tightens, with every answer grounded in linked 3D evidence. On $12$ ScanNet scenes evaluated using instance-level official annotations, the anchor-first hierarchy assigns the retrieved object to the proper structural parent where open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs essentially cannot ($0.24$ compared to $0.01$ with matched input), a capability difference instead of an overall win. The queryable index has a cost of $14$\,KB per scene without the linked evidence frames, and we make available the suites, memories and code.

    ENGLISH

    Agentic systems, AI architectures that autonomously execute multi-step workflows to achieve complex goals, are often built using repeated large language model (LLM) calls for closed-set decision tasks such as routing, shortlisting, gating, and verification. While convenient, this design makes deployments slow and expensive due to cumulative latency and token usage. We propose TabAgent, a framework for replacing generative decision components in closed-set selection tasks with a compact textual-tabular classifier trained on execution traces. TabAgent (i) extracts structured schema, state, and dependency features from trajectories (TabSchema), (ii) augments coverage with schema-aligned synthetic supervision (TabSynth), and (iii) scores candidates with a lightweight classifier (TabHead). On the long-horizon AppWorld benchmark, TabAgent maintains task-level success while eliminating shortlist-time LLM calls, reducing latency by approximately 95% and inference cost by 85-91%. Beyond tool shortlisting, TabAgent generalizes to other agentic decision heads, establishing a paradigm for learned discriminative replacements of generative bottlenecks in production agent architectures.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    In multi-turn conversations, large language models typically condition on the full conversation history: both past user prompts and assistant responses. We revisit this design choice by comparing full-context prompting to four alternative, substantially-reduced context configurations. Analyzing in-the-wild multi-turn conversations across three open reasoning and one state-of-the-art model, we find that response quality is largely preserved under aggressive context filtering: replacing all prior assistant turns with one-sentence summaries or keeping only the most recent user--assistant exchange often matches storing full context in performance while using roughly 8x less context. To understand this result, we observe that a substantial fraction of user turns (36.4%) in multi-turn conversations are self-contained and that many follow-up turns can be addressed by seeing only the immediately preceding user--assistant exchange. Furthermore, we find that when models condition on their own past responses, this can lead to context pollution, a phenomenon in which reasoning errors, hallucinations, or stylistic artifacts propagate across turns. Motivated by these findings, we design a context-filtering approach that selectively omits the assistant-side history. Taken together, these findings suggest moving away from storing full dialogue transcripts and instead retaining only what is relevant.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    ENGLISH

    On-policy agents discard trajectories after each update, including rare high-return episodes. We propose Optimistic Policy Regularization (OPR), which turns those episodes into a closed-form reward bonus: we estimate an elite action prior from top-quartile episodes and add a \reviewblue{bounded transform of the log-ratio} of the prior to the policy's action distribution. OPR needs no auxiliary network, value gate, off-policy correction, or adversarial loop. It is a one-line modification of Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)'s reward; yet, on 49 Atari games at 10M steps, $5\times$ fewer agent decisions than the 200M-frame baselines, it reaches a 148.4\% median human-normalized score (HNS; 196.9\% interquartile mean): higher scores than published PPO on $36/49$ games ($p{=}0.0014$) and a higher aggregate median than self-imitation learning, which falls well below OPR when frames and backbone are matched. We pair the method with a theory of when it works. The underlying log-ratio has an exact forward-KL interpretation; its pre-advantage placement propagates the signal through Generalized Advantage Estimation; and, under an idealized local update, its first-order effect depends on a prior-advantage alignment whose sign indicates help or harm. Since alignment varies across tasks and runs, we also study an online gating extension. On a ten-game set, it outperforms the backbone by $+17.4$ median HNS on average across seeds. Controlled experiments test temporal propagation and the tradeoffs of state conditioning and gating, supporting OPR as a simple regularizer with an analysis of where to shape.

    ENGLISH

    The performance of machine learning models depends on discovering features in the data that are relevant to solving the given task while ignoring irrelevant variation. To check and visualize whether this is the case, we propose 'invariance auditing', a diagnostic tool to analyze feature extractors. Invariance auditing generates diverse inputs which all yield the same features as a given query input, and are therefore treated as identical by the model. Using external knowledge about the task at hand, this enables assessing if the learned invariances do or do not conform to the task's required semantics. Unlike existing work where a dedicated generative model is trained for each feature extractor, our algorithm is training-free and exploits a pretrained diffusion or flow-matching model to sample invariant inputs. Our fiber loss -- which penalizes feature mismatch -- guides the denoising process so the output shares the same representation as the query input. This replaces days of training with a single guided generation procedure at comparable quality. Experiments on popular datasets and model types demonstrate that our auditing method reveals invariances spanning very desirable and concerning behavior. For instance, it detects cases where Qwen-2B places patients with situs inversus (heart on the right side) in the same fiber as typical anatomy.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Recent work provides overwhelming evidence that LLMs, even those trained to scale their reasoning trace, quickly deteriorate at planning as problems become more complex. LLM-as-Formalizers aim to address this by employing LLMs as a bridge to translate natural language descriptions into structured planning representations such as PDDL, which are then fed to a programmatic solver. We observe that its success may be overstated because planning problem descriptions in standard benchmarks often have a one-to-one mapping to PDDL, which departs from real use cases. To address this, we introduce the notion of unraveling problems where a natural yet succinct description translates into a very large PDDL representation. Using unraveling variants of four standard planning domains, we demonstrate that LLM Formalizers also do not always scale. We tackle this challenge by introducing a new paradigm, LLM-as-Higher-Order-Formalizer, where the LLM generates a high-level program that captures the recurrent logic within the description and in turn generates the larger PDDL representation. This decouples token output from the combinatorial explosion of the underlying formalization and search space, leading to improved performance for complex problems.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Claude Code's auto mode is the first deployed permission system for AI coding agents, using a two-stage transcript classifier to gate dangerous tool calls. Anthropic reports a 0.4% false positive rate and 17% false negative rate on production traffic. We present the first independent evaluation of this system on deliberately ambiguous authorization scenarios, i.e., tasks where the user's intent is clear but the target scope, blast radius, or risk level is underspecified. Using AmPermBench, a 128-prompt benchmark spanning four DevOps task families and three controlled ambiguity axes, we evaluate 253 state-changing actions at the individual action level against oracle ground truth. Our findings characterize auto mode's scope-escalation coverage under this stress-test workload. The end-to-end false negative rate is 81.0% (95% CI: 73.8%-87.4%), substantially higher than the 17% reported on production traffic, reflecting a fundamentally different workload rather than a contradiction. Notably, 36.8% of all state-changing actions fall outside the classifier's scope via Tier 2 (in-project file edits), contributing to the elevated end-to-end FNR. Even restricting to the 160 actions the classifier actually evaluates (Tier 3), the FNR remains 70.3%, while the FPR rises to 31.9%. The Tier 2 coverage gap is most pronounced on artifact cleanup (92.9% FNR), where agents naturally fall back to editing state files when the expected CLI is unavailable. These results highlight a coverage boundary worth examining: auto mode assumes dangerous actions transit the shell, but agents routinely achieve equivalent effects through file edits that the classifier does not evaluate.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language model agents rely on effective model context to obtain task-relevant information for decision-making. Many existing context engineering approaches primarily rely on the context generated from the past experience and retrieval mechanisms that reuse these context. However, retrieved context from past tasks must be adapted by the execution agent to fit new situations, placing additional reasoning burden on the underlying LLM. To address this limitation, we propose a generative context augmentation framework using Contrastive Learning of Experience via Agentic Reflection (CLEAR). CLEAR first employs a reflection agent to perform contrastive analysis over past execution trajectories and summarize useful context for each observed task. These summaries are then used as supervised fine-tuning data to train a context augmentation model (CAM). Then we further optimize CAM using reinforcement learning, where the reward signal is obtained by running the task execution agent. By learning to generate task-specific knowledge rather than retrieve knowledge from the past, CAM produces context that is better tailored to the current task. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on the AppWorld and WebShop benchmarks. Experimental results show that CLEAR consistently outperforms strong baselines. It improves task completion rate from 72.62% to 81.15% on AppWorld test set and averaged reward from 0.68 to 0.74 on a subset of WebShop, compared with baseline agent. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/awslabs/CLEAR.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    We investigate whether an explicit learned memory graph can replace the Feed-Forward Network (FFN) sublayer in a decoder-only transformer while preserving the surrounding autoregressive architecture. In the proposed graph Memory Transformer (GMT), a memory cell routes token representations over a learned bank of centroids connected by a learned directed transition matrix, while causal self-attention remains unchanged. In the base v7 instantiation, each of 16 transformer blocks contains 128 centroids and a 128 x 128 edge matrix. Each cell uses gravitational source routing and token-conditioned target selection to return a gated displacement from the estimated source memory state toward the target memory state, rather than a retrieved value. The resulting decoder-only language model has 82.2M trainable parameters and no dense FFN sublayers; the evaluated dense GPT-style baseline has 103.0M. It trains stably and exposes centroid usage, transition structure, and source-to-target movement for direct inspection in the forward computation. It trails the larger baseline in validation loss and perplexity (3.5995/36.58 vs. 3.2903/26.85), while showing close zero-shot benchmark behavior under the evaluated setting. These results support the viability and structural interpretability of replacing dense within-token transformation with graph-mediated memory navigation, without claiming state-of-the-art performance. Broader scaling, optimized kernels, and more extensive benchmark evaluation remain for future work.

    Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials play a fundamental role in computational chemistry and materials science, enabling applications from molecular dynamics simulations to drug design and materials discovery. While recent approaches can estimate inter-atomic forces with high precision, it remains unclear to what extent they can generalise to previously unseen molecules. Do they learn the compositional structure of chemistry, capturing how molecular fragments and their combinations determine properties, or do they primarily learn to interpolate patterns that are specific to the training examples? To address this question, we propose a benchmark consisting of four tasks that require some form of compositional generalisation. In each task, models are tested on molecules that were unseen during training, but the training data is chosen such that generalisation to the test examples should be feasible for models that learn the underlying physical principles.     Graph combinatorial optimization (GCO) has attracted growing interest, as many NP-hard problems naturally admit graph formulations, yet their combinatorial explosion renders exact methods computationally intractable. Recent advances in Reinforcement Learning (RL) combined with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have significantly improved learning-based GCO solvers. However, existing approaches face limitations in both generalization across diverse graph instances and computational scalability as action spaces grow. To address both challenges, we introduce \textit{projection agents}, a GCO methodology built on the Wolpertinger framework and adapted to a shared GNN-based latent space for observations and actions. These agents are trained to solve GCO problems by predicting a desired latent action in a single forward pass, which is subsequently decoded into a valid discrete action in the graph using the latent space. Across diverse benchmarks, our approach achieves up to 6.41$\times$ faster inference and up to 75\% better generalization than existing solutions using a simple nearest-neighbor decoding, while opening the door to strong RL performance in super-linear decision spaces with multiple interdependent variables. Finally, we release \texttt{LaGCO-RL}, a Python library that automates latent action-space construction and supports existing RL-GCO solutions, promoting reproducibility and adaptation to new GCO benchmarks.

    Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning can improve LLM performance, but its benefits vary across tasks, models, and individual queries. On some tasks, CoT provides marginal or negative accuracy gains while substantially increasing token consumption. We investigate whether early decoding dynamics can help identify when explicit reasoning is useful. Our analysis shows that tasks with larger CoT gains tend to exhibit decreasing early-stage entropy, while low-gain tasks more often show oscillatory or increasing trajectories. These patterns motivate an empirical regime interpretation of decoding behavior. We propose \textbf{EDRM} (Entropy Dynamics-based Reasoning Manifold), a lightweight routing framework whose default heuristic requires no router training. EDRM summarizes early entropy trajectories with a compact, interpretable representation and selects among Direct, Standard, and CoT decoding. Across 15 benchmarks and 7 LLMs, its global and instance-level variants offer \textbf{16--55\%} token savings at comparable accuracy. The Full instance-level configuration combines routing with a short Direct fallback branch; our heuristic-router ablation reports up to \textbf{4.9 percentage points} of additional accuracy from oracle answer selection over routing without fallback. These results support selective reasoning based on early decoding signals and demonstrate the potential of entropy-based control for efficient LLM inference.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    An activation oracle is a language model trained to convert the activations of another model into natural language. However, it is so far unclear to what extent these verbalizations are calibrated. Crucially, the oracle's verbalization come without any measure of confidence. Here, we compare five methods for estimating the confidence of an activation oracle. Our experiments cover four oracles from two model families (Qwen and Gemma, from 8B to 27B parameters), tested on the secret word task, whereby the oracle is supposed to recover a secret word, that has been fine-tuned into a model but does not appear in the model outputs. Our results with $6{,}000$ samples per method/oracle combination show that the best calibration depends on the availability of a hypothesis space or a calibration set: When an assumed auditor can list the possible answers in advance, the oracle should score each candidate answer directly. Scoring the candidates gives a higher accuracy on every oracle and a confidence that separates correct from incorrect answers better than any other method. When the oracle has to write its answer as free text, the agreement over twenty sampled answers gives the best calibrated confidence, which needs only five labeled secret words to be tuned. When a calibration set is available, a rescaled probability of the answer is as good as re-sampling, at the cost of one generation instead of twenty. Asking the oracle to write a number for its confidence, on the other side, gives no useful signal on any oracle. Code and the patched trainer are available at https://github.com/federicotorrielli/probabilistic_activation_oracles.

    Post-trained language models often exhibit a recognizable AI-like writing style, yet its connection to post-training and internal representations remains poorly understood. In this work, we study whether post-training introduces or amplifies AI-like stylistic regularities and whether these regularities have a localized internal signature. To this end, we compare human text, base-model generations, and aligned-model generations under matched human-source prefixes. Aligned generations show lower human-corpus affinity and higher AI-detection rates than base generations, suggesting that post-training shifts generated text away from human-corpus style and toward detector-visible AI-like text. We then introduce PASTA (Post-training Alignment Signature Targeted Ablation), a training-free method that estimates a post-training alignment signature from aligned-base residual contrasts and ablates the corresponding direction during decoding. Across 11 aligned models and 6 AI-detectors, PASTA lowers the detection rate for most aligned models; this effect transfers well across detectors and is not reproduced by random directions. Qualitative analysis suggests that PASTA generations remain relevant and coherent while exhibiting greater stylistic variation. Together, these results show that AI-like stylistic effects of post-training can be measured, localized, and causally tested through activation ablation.

    Vision-language models (VLMs) deliver strong multimodal reasoning capabilities, but their large computational cost and high parameter counts make deployment challenging on resource-constrained devices. Low-rank decomposition has emerged as a promising compression technique, yet existing methods often optimize local matrix reconstruction error, rely on uniform or heuristic rank allocation, and focus mainly on attention projections while leaving feed-forward networks underexplored. In this paper, we propose~\textit{LASER} (\textbf{L}oss-\textbf{A}ware \textbf{S}ingular-value d\textbf{E}composition and \textbf{R}ank allocation), a low-rank compression framework for efficient low-precision VLM inference. LASER derives a curvature-weighted SVD objective from a second-order approximation of the model loss and uses Kronecker-factored Fisher information to guide decomposition toward downstream performance rather than reconstruction alone. We further introduce a loss-aware cross-layer rank allocation strategy based on calibration gradients, enabling more effective parameter budgeting across layers. Finally, we extend low-rank compression to FFN layers through a hybrid scheme that combines SVD with quantization. The evaluation results show that LASER achieves more than $2.3\times$ decoding speedup over previous work while preserving strong accuracy under low-precision inference.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper formalizes and tests how serving-kernel differences affect model behavior, with bounds for distribution shifts, reward, policy-gradient bias, and token changes, plus traffic-specific kernel contracts. This is a substantial contribution to inference-system design; behavioral change is incidental to mechanistic interpretability, while its reward and policy-gradient analysis gives a partial connection to reasoning-related training.

    本文形式化并检验了服务内核差异如何影响模型行为，提出了关于分布偏移、奖励、策略梯度偏差和 token 变化的界，以及针对具体流量的内核契约。这对推理系统设计作出了实质性贡献；行为变化只是附带涉及机制可解释性，而奖励和策略梯度分析则与推理相关训练有部分联系。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    A trained model is usually described by its weights, as if the weights fixed its behavior. In practice the same weights are run by different programs. Training uses high-precision accumulation and fixed tensor shapes, while serving uses low-precision arithmetic, fused attention kernels, a paged key-value cache, and dynamic batching. These programs produce different next-token distributions from identical weights. We make this dependence explicit by indexing a policy by the kernel that executes it, and we propose kernel contracts, which state how far a serving kernel may drift from a reference kernel on each slice of traffic and what the serving system should do when a limit is exceeded. We prove non-asymptotic bounds that link the logit difference between two kernels to total-variation and KL divergence, to the change in expected reward, to the bias of policy gradients computed from rollouts generated by another kernel, and to whether the greedy token can change. We test the bounds and the contracts in GPU experiments on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with Hugging Face and vLLM. The bounds hold on every prompt we measured. Lower precision, a different serving engine, and a different batch size each change the generated token on some prompts, and these changes concentrate on prompts where the model is nearly undecided between two tokens. A kernel can therefore look fine on aggregate metrics while behaving differently on exactly these prompts. Checking a contract separately on each slice of traffic catches these cases.

    中文

    通常，人们用模型权重来描述一个训练好的模型，仿佛权重决定了其行为。实际上，同一组权重会由不同程序运行。训练使用高精度累加和固定张量形状，而服务阶段使用低精度算术、融合注意力内核、分页式键值缓存和动态批处理。这些程序会从相同的权重产生不同的下一个 token 概率分布。我们通过按执行策略的内核为策略建立索引，明确表达这种依赖关系，并提出内核契约，规定服务内核在每个流量切片上相对于参考内核允许出现多大偏差，以及超过限值时服务系统应采取什么措施。我们证明了非渐近界，将两个内核之间的 logit 差异与总变差和 KL 散度、期望奖励的变化、利用另一个内核生成的 rollout 计算出的策略梯度偏差，以及贪心选择的 token 是否会改变联系起来。我们使用 Hugging Face 和 vLLM，在 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 上通过 GPU 实验检验这些界和契约。对于我们测量的每个提示词，这些界都成立。较低的精度、不同的服务引擎和不同的批处理大小，都会在一些提示词上改变生成的 token；这些变化集中出现在模型难以在两个 token 之间作出选择的提示词上。因此，某个内核在总体指标上看似表现良好，却可能恰好在这些提示词上产生不同的行为。针对每个流量切片分别检查契约，就能捕捉到这些情况。

    PERIA develops and trains a visual agent that uses tools to gather and verify evidence for multi-step spatial reasoning, with benchmark gains as evidence. This directly advances reasoning and agent systems; the abstract does not describe internal model mechanisms, and spatial task coverage alone provides only an incidental connection to compositional generalization.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    While recent vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate strong multimodal understanding, they remain limited in spatial reasoning tasks that require active evidence acquisition and multi-step visual interaction. This limitation suggests that relying solely on implicit visual representations from vision encoders is insufficient for recovering fine-grained spatial evidence. We introduce PERception-Interaction-reason Agent (PERIA), a tool-augmented visual agent for spatial reasoning tasks across map reasoning, visual probing, and vision reconstruction. PERIA uses two lightweight tool families: vision perception tools for exposing textual, symbolic, and spatial evidence, and vision interaction tools for manipulating visual context, tracing paths, and verifying spatial relations. To train PERIA, we develop a unified recipe that combines supervised tool-use trajectory synthesis, composite rewards, and Observation-Relaxed Group-in-Group Policy Optimization (OR-GIGPO) for effective multi-tool behavior. Experiments on 13 benchmarks from 8 datasets show that PERIA-8B improves over the Qwen3-8B backbone by 10.0 percentage points on in-distribution benchmarks and 4.4 percentage points on out-of-distribution benchmarks, while outperforming previous state-of-the-art baselines of similar size by 6.9--14.8 percentage points. It also achieves performance comparable to much larger models such as Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking and GPT-5, demonstrating the effectiveness of PERIA in enhancing spatial reasoning capabilities.

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Motion instruction generation in cross-video comparison aims to produce corrective feedback that describes the differences between a query and a reference motion. However, existing models often generate instructions that exhibit motion hallucinations, failing to reflect actual kinematic differences between paired videos. To systematically investigate these hallucinations, we introduce MotionHalluc, a dedicated benchmark for evaluating motion hallucinations in paired-video comparison. MotionHalluc comprises 1540 fine-grained questions over 553 video pairs, evaluating hallucinations along three core dimensions: (1)directional hallucination, (2)attributional hallucination, and (3)temporal hallucination. Extensive evaluations of state-of-the-art large multimodal models demonstrate high susceptibility to these hallucinations. Furthermore, we provide Perceive-Parse-Verify (PPV) as a training-free measurements extraction and verification baseline that converts candidate instructions into executable measurement queries and supplies kinematic measurements at inference time. Our results show that this simple measurements injection yields an average 10.6% performance gain across models, suggesting that motion reasoning with explicit quantitative measurements is a key factor in reducing hallucinations in cross-video comparison. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Leocoding0971/MotionHalluc.

    中文

    在跨视频比较中，运动指令生成旨在产生纠正性反馈，描述查询动作与参考动作之间的差异。然而，现有模型经常生成带有运动幻觉的指令，未能反映成对视频之间实际的运动学差异。为系统研究这些幻觉，我们提出 MotionHalluc，这是一个专门评估成对视频比较中运动幻觉的基准。MotionHalluc 包含针对 553 对视频的 1540 个细粒度问题，从三个核心维度评估幻觉：（1）方向幻觉，（2）归因幻觉，以及（3）时间幻觉。对最先进大型多模态模型的大量评估表明，它们很容易产生此类幻觉。此外，我们提出 Perceive-Parse-Verify（PPV），这是一种无需训练的测量提取与验证基线方法：它将候选指令转换为可执行的测量查询，并在推理时提供运动学测量。结果表明，这种简单的测量注入使各模型的平均性能提升了 10.6%，说明在跨视频比较中，基于显式定量测量的运动推理是减少幻觉的关键因素。我们的代码和数据集见 https://github.com/Leocoding0971/MotionHalluc。

    ManimAgent：用于视觉教育的自我进化多模态智能体

    Wenjia Jiang, Zongyuan Cai, Yuanhang Shao, Chenru Wang, Boyan Han, Zhixue Song, Keyu Chen, Shengwei An, Xu Yang, and Zhou Yang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    ManimAgent’s main contribution is a dual-channel episodic memory that carries validated successes and failures across code-generation tasks, with evaluation showing gains as memory grows. This substantially advances agent memory design; the animation task and reflection process provide application context but do not establish a core advance in compositional generalization or reasoning mechanisms.

    ManimAgent 的主要贡献是一个双通道情景记忆机制，可在代码生成任务之间传递经验证的成功经验与失败经验；评估表明，随着记忆增大，性能有所提升。这实质性推动了智能体记忆设计的发展；动画任务和反思过程提供了应用背景，但并未构成组合泛化或推理机制方面的核心进展。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Multi-round reflection lets agents built on large language models recover from failures within a single task, but each task remains an isolated episode: lessons learned across many reflection rounds on one task are discarded before the next begins. We study this gap on a code-generation task: from a scientific paper section, the agent writes Python in the open-source Manim library to render a mathematical animation. We present ManimAgent, a self-evolving multimodal agent that carries reflection experience across tasks through a dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank grown entirely from its own task stream, with no weight updates and no human seeds. After each animation converges, a vision-language model scores the rendered keyframes; the resulting signals populate a positive channel M+ that stores success rationales as soft Reference Examples, and a negative channel M- that stores validated failure patterns as hard Known Pitfalls. On a fixed-probe evaluation against no-memory, matched-budget retrieval-augmented generation, and shuffled-memory baselines, blind human Pass@1 rises and reflection rounds fall as memory size grows.

    中文

    多轮反思使基于大型语言模型的智能体能够在单个任务中从失败中恢复，但每个任务仍是一个孤立的阶段：在一个任务中经过多轮反思学到的经验，会在下一个任务开始前被丢弃。我们在一项代码生成任务中研究这一问题：智能体根据科学论文的一个章节，用开源 Manim 库编写 Python 代码，以渲染数学动画。我们提出 ManimAgent，这是一个自我进化的多模态智能体，它通过双通道情景记忆库将反思经验跨任务延续；该记忆库完全由智能体自身的任务流构建，无需更新权重，也无需人工提供种子。每段动画收敛后，一个视觉语言模型会对渲染出的关键帧评分；所得信号填充正向通道 M+，其中以软参考示例的形式存储成功理由，以及负向通道 M-，其中以硬性已知陷阱的形式存储经验证的失败模式。在固定探测评估中，与无记忆、预算匹配的检索增强生成和打乱记忆基线相比，随着记忆规模增大，盲评人工 Pass@1 提高，反思轮数减少。

    The paper contributes a closed-loop humanoid planning and control framework, with a curriculum for learning error recovery and asynchronous replanning. Its main advance is agent control and computation scheduling; motion coordination alone offers only incidental evidence about compositional reasoning.

    本文提出了一个人形机器人闭环规划与控制框架，其中包含用于学习错误恢复的课程和异步重规划机制。其主要进展在于智能体控制和计算调度；动作协调本身只能为组合推理提供附带证据。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    While current Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) provide robust control priors for humanoids, they only execute pre-defined reference motions. As a result, they are vulnerable to environmental shifts and incapable of reactive whole-body coordination. Naively cascading them with generative motion planners fails to achieve true reactivity, as inevitable tracking discrepancies induce fatal cumulative exposure bias. To bridge this gap, we propose ReactiveBFM, a real-time closed-loop planning-control framework. At its core, we effectively mitigate exposure bias via a scheduled prefix sampling curriculum, forcing the generative planner to actively learn error-recovery behaviors from imperfect physical states rather than ground-truth trajectories. Systematically, to reconcile the severe latency mismatch between auto-regressive planning and high-frequency tracking, we introduce an asynchronous replanning mechanism. Combined with trajectory chunking to temporally ensemble spatial references, our system guarantees spatio-temporally fluid execution without physical jitter. Deployed on the Unitree G1 humanoid, ReactiveBFM demonstrates unprecedented physical agility across a vast repertoire of text-conditioned closed-loop motions. Notably, ReactiveBFM achieves zero-shot moving target reaching, showcasing intricate whole-body coordination and on-the-fly replanning. In sim-to-sim benchmarking under severe perturbations, ReactiveBFM achieves a 93.1% success rate, significantly outperforming cascaded open-loop baselines by 28.6%.

    中文

    尽管当前的行为基础模型（BFM）为人形机器人提供了稳健的控制先验，但它们只能执行预定义的参考动作。因此，它们容易受到环境变化的影响，也无法实现反应式全身协调。将其简单地与生成式运动规划器串接，仍无法实现真正的反应能力，因为不可避免的跟踪偏差会引发致命的累积暴露偏差。为弥合这一差距，我们提出 ReactiveBFM，这是一个实时闭环规划控制框架。其核心是通过定时前缀采样课程有效缓解暴露偏差，迫使生成式规划器从不完美的物理状态而非真实轨迹中主动学习错误恢复行为。为系统解决自回归规划与高频跟踪之间严重的延迟不匹配问题，我们引入异步重规划机制。结合轨迹分块，对空间参考进行时间集成，使系统能够保证时空流畅的执行，避免物理抖动。ReactiveBFM 部署在 Unitree G1 人形机器人上，在大量由文本条件控制的闭环动作中展现出前所未有的身体敏捷性。值得注意的是，ReactiveBFM 实现了零样本移动目标抵达，展现出复杂的全身协调和即时重规划能力。在严重扰动条件下的仿真到仿真基准测试中，ReactiveBFM 的成功率达到 93.1%，比串接式开环基线高出 28.6%。

    WhisperRec：面向高效基础推荐模型的潜在推理

    Hao Jiang, Peiru Du, Pengfei Yao, Mengting Li, Siyuan Lou, Kuo Cai, Sheng Yu, Qiang Luo, Jian Liang, Ruiming Tang, Fei Pan, Peng Jiang, Wenwu Ou

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    WhisperRec trains recommendation models to internalize teacher CoT as latent tokens, making efficient latent reasoning its main contribution. This gives partial insight into reasoning and learned representations, but the abstract does not analyze internal mechanisms or compositional generalization; inference efficiency is a secondary systems benefit.

    WhisperRec 训练推荐模型将教师 CoT 内化为潜在 token，因此其主要贡献是高效的潜在推理。这在一定程度上揭示了推理和学习到的表示，但摘要没有分析内部机制或组合泛化；推理效率是次要的系统收益。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong reasoning capabilities, motivating their adoption as backbones for foundation recommendation models (FRMs). Existing approaches typically enhance recommendation with explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) under the Think-then-Answer paradigm. However, generating lengthy rationales introduces substantial inference overhead, while fixed CoT templates struggle to model diverse, dynamic, and context-dependent user interests. We propose WhisperRec, an efficient latent reasoning framework for FRMs. WhisperRec compresses teacher-generated CoT into learnable latent reasoning tokens, enabling a Latent-Reason-then-Answer paradigm that performs reasoning in latent space without producing verbose rationales. This design retains decision-relevant reasoning information while avoiding the latency bottleneck of autoregressive rationale generation. Specifically, it first introduces Multi-View Adaptive CoT (MV-ACoT) to construct diverse, high-quality supervision from complementary perspectives on user interests. MV-ACoT also adapts reasoning complexity to each instance, applying lightweight analysis to clear cases and targeted multi-factor reasoning to challenging ones. Building on a pre-trained FRM, WhisperRec then employs a three-stage Latent Reasoning Alignment procedure to progressively internalize teacher CoT into latent representations. Finally, curriculum-based post-training activates latent-token reasoning for downstream recommendation while preserving standard recommendation capability. Experiments on an industrial-scale Kuaishou dataset and the public Kuaishou LLM-Rec benchmark show that WhisperRec consistently outperforms explicit-CoT methods and conventional baselines. Compared with explicit CoT Think and No-Think variants, WhisperRec improves SID@64 by 17.44% and 9.33%, respectively, and achieves over 10x higher online inference throughput.

    中文

    大型语言模型（LLM）展现出强大的推理能力，因此人们开始将其用作基础推荐模型（FRM）的骨干网络。现有方法通常在“先思考后回答”范式下，通过显式思维链（CoT）增强推荐能力。然而，生成冗长的推理过程会带来显著的推理开销，而固定的 CoT 模板难以建模多样、动态且依赖上下文的用户兴趣。我们提出 WhisperRec，一种面向 FRM 的高效潜在推理框架。WhisperRec 将教师生成的 CoT 压缩为可学习的潜在推理 token，从而实现“先潜在推理后回答”范式，在潜在空间中进行推理，而无需生成冗长的推理过程。这种设计保留了与决策相关的推理信息，同时避免了自回归生成推理过程造成的延迟瓶颈。具体而言，WhisperRec 首先引入多视角自适应 CoT（MV-ACoT），从互补视角构建多样且高质量的用户兴趣监督信号。MV-ACoT 还会根据每个实例调整推理复杂度：对明确的情况进行轻量分析，对有挑战的情况进行有针对性的多因素推理。随后，WhisperRec 基于预训练 FRM，采用三阶段潜在推理对齐流程，逐步将教师 CoT 内化到潜在表示中。最后，基于课程学习的后训练激活潜在 token 推理，用于下游推荐，同时保留标准推荐能力。在工业规模的快手数据集和公开的快手 LLM-Rec 基准上的实验表明，WhisperRec 持续优于显式 CoT 方法和传统基线。与显式 CoT 的 Think 和 No-Think 变体相比，WhisperRec 的 SID@64 分别提升了 17.44% 和 9.33%，在线推理吞吐量则超过其 10 倍。

    Stef Cuyckens, Mihaela Jivanescu, Jun Yin, Chao Fang, Marian Verhelst

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    Ares adapts LLM reasoning effort during RTL optimization, with a patience-based policy that improves design quality at a given cost. The effort-allocation algorithm advances systems and is related to reasoning optimization, but the abstract does not study reasoning mechanisms or compositionality.

    Ares 在 RTL 优化过程中自适应调整 LLM 的推理力度，并通过基于耐心计数的策略，以给定成本提升设计质量。这种推理力度分配算法推进了系统技术，也与推理优化相关，但摘要没有研究推理机制或组合性。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Large language model (LLM) agents optimize the power, performance, and area (PPA) of register-transfer-level (RTL) designs by iterating over edits, synthesis, and PPA analysis, paying a dollar cost for every LLM call. Prior agents report the quality reached without its normalized cost, attribute that quality to an engineered cross-design memory, and hold the reasoning effort of every call fixed. We propose Ares with three corresponding innovations. (1) We introduce a normalized dollar cost per LLM call reported alongside the figure of merit (FoM), enabling fair comparison across effort levels and optimizers. (2) Using this accounting, we find the construction of the long-term memory matters little. An engineered memory brings no dependable gain over a plain concatenation of the same experience. (3) We instead adapt the per-call reasoning effort by escalating to deeper reasoning only once progress at a lower effort stalls, via a patience counter fit on 21 training designs, allocating reasoning where it pays rather than uniformly across all iterations. On three test designs unseen during training, the effort policy lowers the FoM by 22-28% with Opus 4.6 and by 18-34% with GPT-5.5, where the best fixed effort reaches 20-24% and 19-29%, respectively, at equal normalized cost. Ares closes on average 91% of the gap from an LLM-drafted multiply-accumulate unit to its highly hand-optimized counterpart. It also reaches a 5% lower FoM than state-of-the-art Dr. RTL at only 35% of its cost.

    大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通过反复修改、综合和分析 PPA 来优化寄存器传输级（RTL）设计，每次调用 LLM 都需要支付费用。以往的智能体报告达到的质量，却不报告其标准化成本；它们将该质量归因于专门设计的跨设计记忆，并且每次调用的推理力度都固定不变。我们提出 Ares，包含三项相应的创新。（1）我们引入每次 LLM 调用的标准化费用，并与评价指标（FoM）一同报告，从而能够公平比较不同推理力度和优化器。（2）借助这种核算方式，我们发现长期记忆的构建方式影响不大。与对相同经验进行简单串接相比，专门设计的记忆没有带来可靠的增益。（3）我们改为自适应地调整每次调用的推理力度：只有当较低力度下的进展停滞时，才逐步提升到更深入的推理；具体通过在 21 个训练设计上拟合的耐心计数器来实现，使推理资源投向能产生收益之处，而非均匀分配到所有迭代中。在训练期间未见过的三个测试设计上，该推理力度策略使用相同的标准化成本时，使 Opus 4.6 的 FoM 降低 22–28%，使 GPT-5.5 的 FoM 降低 18–34%；最佳固定推理力度分别达到 20–24% 和 19–29% 的降幅。Ares 平均弥合了 LLM 起草的乘加单元与高度手工优化版本之间 91% 的差距。它还以仅 35% 的成本，实现了比最先进的 Dr. RTL 低 5% 的 FoM。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper proposes graph-guided LLM design of complete heuristic pipelines, with path-dependent credit assignment, and evaluates it on combinatorial optimization problems. Algorithm design and credit assignment relate to reasoning, but the abstract centers on pipeline search rather than how models reason, so that connection is limited; its main contribution is a transferable algorithmic system-design method.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    The rapid development of Large Language Models (LLMs) has opened new avenues for Automated Heuristic Design (AHD) for solving NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). However, existing LLM-driven AHD methods are largely confined to rigid solver templates, relegating the search process to isolated module tuning. Transitioning to fully autonomous, system-level algorithm design is essential but fraught with low reliability of generated operators, extremely large search spaces, and ineffective credit assignment. To overcome these drawbacks, this paper proposes a Directed Graph-Guided Automated Algorithm Design framework, termed DGA$_2$D. It structures the open-ended program space as a directed graph, where each node represents a functional operator that can be instantiated using one of multiple candidate code implementations, while directed walks constitute complete algorithmic pipelines. A first-order path-dependent credit assignment mechanism is introduced to evaluate code variations strictly based on their topological context. Extensive experiments across 12 distinct COPs, ranging from complex scheduling to routing, demonstrate the consistent empirical advantages of DGA$_2$D. It reduces the average normalized gap by up to 10.96 percentage points compared to state-of-the-art LLM baselines.

    Shreyas Kowshik, Sreyas Venkataraman, Leo Wang, Niharika Pant, Max Simchowitz and Aviral Kumar

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper develops MiDAS, combining few-demonstration behavior cloning with value-based residual learning over frozen VLA representations, and identifies design principles for reliable online robot adaptation. Its central contribution advances learning and problem-solving through reinforcement learning, while the representations are used as a substrate rather than analyzed mechanistically; adaptation and skill transfer are not explicitly framed as compositional generalization, and no new agent architecture is established.

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    A central goal in robot learning is to move beyond task-specific human data collection toward robots that improve through autonomous interaction. Yet fully autonomous learning remains difficult with current policies: sparse rewards and weak zero-shot exploration often prevent online learning from discovering successful behavior. As a first step towards fully autonomous learning, we propose the minimal-data adaptation regime, in which a pretrained robot policy must learn a new task from as little as one demonstration followed by autonomous online interaction. We establish that, although pretrained policies fail zero-shot on many new tasks, a single demonstration suffices to direct their behavioral prior to coarse task-following behavior, albeit with unreliable performance. From this insight, we isolate the key design principles required to convert coarse task-following into reliable task success. These include (1) the surprising efficacy of pretrained VLA representations to support sample-efficient value learning from online interaction (2) the sufficiency of residual policy learning to learn corrective behavior and (3) the need for careful data-balancing to prevent exploration collapse. As a representative of these principles, we propose MiDAS, a simple offline-to-online RL recipe that combines few-demonstration behavior cloning with value-based residual learning over frozen VLA representations. Across LIBERO and RoboCasa tasks, MiDAS substantially improves performance from single-demonstration initializations, including policies that succeed only rarely, validating the principles highlighted above. On a bimanual YAM platform, starting from a brittle initial policy, MiDAS improves task success after approximately six hours of online interaction.

    机器人学习的核心目标之一，是摆脱针对特定任务收集人工数据的模式，转而让机器人通过自主交互不断改进。然而，使用当前策略实现完全自主学习仍然很困难：稀疏奖励和较弱的零样本探索能力，常常使在线学习无法发现成功行为。作为迈向完全自主学习的第一步，我们提出最少数据适应范式：预训练机器人策略只需一次演示，随后通过自主在线交互，就必须学会一项新任务。我们证实，尽管预训练策略在许多新任务上无法零样本完成任务，但单次演示足以引导其行为先验，使其粗略地遵循任务要求，尽管表现并不可靠。基于这一发现，我们归纳出将粗略任务跟随转化为可靠任务成功所需的关键设计原则，包括：（1）预训练 VLA 表示在支持通过在线交互进行样本高效价值学习方面，效果出乎意料地好；（2）残差策略学习足以学会纠正性行为；（3）需要谨慎平衡数据，以防探索崩溃。作为这些原则的代表，我们提出 MiDAS，这是一种简单的离线到在线 RL 方案，将少量演示的行为克隆与基于价值、利用冻结 VLA 表示进行的残差学习相结合。在 LIBERO 和 RoboCasa 任务中，MiDAS 显著提升了从单次演示初始化出发的表现，包括成功率极低的策略，从而验证了上述原则。在双臂 YAM 平台上，以一个脆弱的初始策略为起点，MiDAS 在约六小时的在线交互后提升了任务成功率。

    Utkarsh Bahuguna

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper analyzes when self-consistency voting and confidence signals help or hurt small models’ answers to hard science questions, with preregistered evidence about within-problem confidence. This is a strong empirical contribution to reasoning evaluation, but it does not explain internal mechanisms or advance agent systems.

    本文分析了自一致性投票和置信度信号何时会提升或损害小型模型回答困难科学问题的表现，并通过预注册证据考察逐题置信度。这是对推理评估的重要实证贡献，但没有解释内部机制或推进智能体系统。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Majority-vote self-consistency (SC) lowers per-problem accuracy on most GPQA Diamond problems for small instruction-tuned models: on 56.6% of problems for Qwen2.5-7B and 65.7% for Llama-3-8B. An obvious fix is a verifier-free confidence gate that decides which problems to vote on. We report that the most natural version of that fix also fails, and we separate three signal failures that v1 treated as one. The token-entropy gate fails for a measurement reason: averaged over a chain of 602 tokens, entropy mostly measures fluency. The chain average sits 0.0005 nats from the non-answer average and 0.1695 nats from the answer token. So we measure confidence at the answer token itself. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Turbo (198 problems, 64 samples each), a sample that disagrees with its problem's plurality still emits its answer at a median margin of at least 20.4 nats, and at least 75.5% of such samples exceed 10 nats. Both quantities were pre-registered and tested once on 69 problems that no exploratory analysis had seen; both passed. The unit matters. Pooled across the benchmark, the margin does separate correct from incorrect samples: the fraction above 10 nats differs by +0.0586 [+0.0160, +0.0994]. Within a problem, paired, it does not: -0.0142 [-0.0501, +0.0215]. Token log-probabilities do carry information, but not for the within-question choice that self-consistency makes. The agreement gate's failure has no mechanism we can identify, and we leave it open. The new claims rest on one model: a registered replication on a second model was sampled but could not be evaluated, and we report that instead. Separately, three reasoning models could not be evaluated on hosted serverless inference at a small budget, each for a different measured reason. All three are downloadable, so this is a limit of metered APIs, not of what can be known.

    中文

    多数投票式自一致性（SC）会降低小型指令微调模型在 GPQA Diamond 大多数问题上的逐题准确率：Qwen2.5-7B 有 56.6% 的问题如此，Llama-3-8B 则有 65.7%。一个显而易见的修复办法是使用无需验证器的置信度门控，决定哪些问题采用投票。我们报告说，这种修复办法最自然的版本同样失效，并将 v1 合并处理的三种信号失效情况区分开来。token 熵门控在测量上存在问题：对一条包含 602 个 token 的推理链求平均后，熵主要测量的是流畅度。整条推理链的平均熵与非答案平均值只差 0.0005 nats，与答案 token 则相差 0.1695 nats。因此，我们直接在答案 token 上测量置信度。在 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-Turbo 上（198 个问题，每题 64 个样本），与该问题的众数答案不一致的样本，其答案 token 的发射边际中位数仍至少为 20.4 nats，且至少 75.5% 的此类样本超过 10 nats。这两个量均已预注册，并在 69 个探索性分析从未见过的问题上各测试一次；二者均通过检验。衡量单位很重要。在整个基准上汇总时，该边际确实能区分正确与错误样本：超过 10 nats 的样本比例相差 +0.0586 [+0.0160, +0.0994]。但在问题内部配对比较时，它无法区分：-0.0142 [-0.0501, +0.0215]。token 对数概率确实包含信息，但无法用于自一致性所作的逐题选择。我们无法确定一致性门控为何失效，因此暂不对此下结论。新的主张基于单个模型：我们对第二个模型进行了注册复现并采集了样本，但无法完成评估，因此如实报告这一情况。另外，三个推理模型在小预算的托管式无服务器推理上无法评估，且各自有不同的实测原因。这三个模型都可以下载，因此这是计量计费 API 的限制，而非知识所能达到的极限。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    Mimir’s main contribution is a sub-2B model trained on permissible data using hierarchical recurrent depth, with ablations showing that changing low- versus high-level stack applications affects performance differently.     阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Training capable language models typically relies on web-scale pretraining followed by multi-stage post-training, creating substantial computational and data-governance barriers for settings in which training data must satisfy explicit permissibility constraints. We introduce Mimir, a 1.78B-parameter language model based on the Hierarchical Reasoning Model Text (HRM-Text) architecture, a recurrent-depth transformer whose layers are split into a low-level (L) and a high-level (H) stack that are applied repeatedly in an interleaved schedule. Mimir is trained from random initialization directly on a curated mixture of instruction, reasoning, tool-use, multilingual, and synthetic data: 161 datasets and 70.5B tokens per epoch for Mimir v1, extended to 103B tokens per epoch for its continued-training successor Mimir v1.5, with synthetic replacements for sources that do not satisfy permissibility criteria. Across 20 benchmarks in English, Danish (a low-resource language with ~6M speakers), and Math & Code, Mimir v1.5 attains the highest average score of all sub-2B models in every domain, outperforming both HRM-Text 1B and the looped transformers Ouro 1.4B and Ouro 2.6B, and Mimir matches or exceeds the performance of models of up to 9B parameters, such as Qwen 3.5 9B and Gemma 4 E4B, on the English and Danish averages. Two independent memorisation audits indicate low memorisation risk despite multi-epoch training. Inference-time ablations show that the number of L-stack applications can be changed with graceful degradation, whereas changing the number of H-stack applications breaks the model. Our results provide evidence that hierarchical recurrent language models can learn effectively from post-training-oriented, permissible data mixtures without conventional web-scale pretraining.

    Huan Zhang, Mingju Chen, Dongxu Zhou, Can Lv, Heng Chang, Sen Cui, Faguo Wu, Shiji Zhou

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    TRCA introduces rubric-based transition rewards to improve credit assignment and policy optimization for long-horizon LLM agents, reporting gains across task benchmarks. This strongly advances agent training and task execution, while stepwise interaction alone offers only a limited connection to compositional generalization and no internal-mechanism analysis.

    TRCA 引入基于评分准则的转移奖励，以改善长时程 LLM 智能体的信用分配和策略优化，并报告了多个任务基准上的提升。这显著推进了智能体训练和任务执行；逐步交互与组合泛化仅有有限关联，也没有对内部机制进行分析。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents are typically optimized with sparse terminal outcomes, making fine-grained credit assignment across multi-step interactions difficult. Existing approaches either rely on process evaluators, which incur annotation and inference costs, or derive step-level credit from successful trajectories. However, successful trajectories are extremely scarce during early-stage reinforcement learning, substantially weakening anchor-based methods. We propose Transition-wise Rubric Credit Assignment (TRCA), which derives step-level supervision directly from action-induced transitions without learned evaluators or successful anchors. TRCA evaluates each transition using Evidence, Execution, and Invalidity rubrics to capture task-relevant information acquisition, valid task execution, and invalid or regressive behavior. From these judgments, Foundational Rubric Reward measures local transition quality, while Breakthrough Rubric Reward tracks newly covered Evidence and Execution conditions to reward incremental task progress. Combined with terminal outcomes, these signals produce fine-grained step-level advantages for policy optimization. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and seven search-augmented question-answering benchmarks show consistent improvements over the evaluated baselines. With Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, TRCA improves the WebShop score by 6.0%-12.6%; with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, it improves the average SearchQA score by 1.9%-18.3%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of transition-wise rubric credit assignment for long-horizon tasks with sparse successful anchors.

    中文

    长时程大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通常通过稀疏的终局结果进行优化，因此难以在多步交互中进行细粒度信用分配。现有方法要么依赖过程评估器，产生标注和推理成本；要么从成功轨迹中推导逐步信用。然而，在强化学习早期阶段，成功轨迹极其稀少，大幅削弱了基于锚点的方法。我们提出逐转移评分准则信用分配（TRCA），直接从动作引起的状态转移中推导逐步监督，无需学习得到的评估器或成功锚点。TRCA 使用 Evidence、Execution 和 Invalidity 三类评分准则评估每次转移，分别捕捉与任务相关的信息获取、有效的任务执行以及无效或退步行为。基于这些判断，Foundational Rubric Reward 衡量局部转移质量，而 Breakthrough Rubric Reward 则追踪新覆盖的 Evidence 和 Execution 条件，以奖励任务的增量进展。将这些信号与终局结果结合后，可为策略优化生成细粒度的逐步优势。在 ALFWorld、WebShop 和七个搜索增强问答基准上的实验表明，该方法持续优于所评估的基线。使用 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 时，TRCA 将 WebShop 得分提升 6.0%–12.6%；使用 Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct 时，将 SearchQA 平均得分提升 1.9%–18.3%。这些结果证明，逐转移评分准则信用分配适用于缺少成功锚点的长时程任务。

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The study shows that entity-specific LoRA adapters can store factual knowledge while semantic or weight-space similarity fails to retrieve it, revealing a storage–retrieval disconnect and motivating query-conditioned adapter composition. This strongly informs mechanisms of knowledge storage and memory design; composition is identified as an open problem rather than demonstrated, and answering factual questions alone does not establish a reasoning contribution.

    研究表明，特定实体的 LoRA 适配器能够存储事实知识，但语义相似度或权重空间相似度无法检索这些知识，揭示了存储与检索之间的脱节，并促使人们探索由查询条件化的适配器组合。这为知识存储机制和记忆设计提供了重要启示；组合仍是被指出的开放问题，并未得到验证，而仅回答事实问题不足以证明其对推理有所贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Graph retrieval-augmented generation places retrieved subgraphs into the model's context window at query time, paying a recurring token cost and exposing source data on every call. We study an alternative: compiling a knowledge graph offline into a bank of LoRA adapters, one per entity, that serve as a parametric knowledge layer queried by injecting weights rather than text, at zero query-time context cost. On the MetaQA dataset, we find that subgraph-trained adapters encode context-free factual knowledge that generalizes to unseen questions: on single-valued relations the adapter gains $+0.243$ exact-match score over a base model that is nearly blind closed-book ($0.007$), and only the correct adapter recovers this knowledge (an oracle gap of $+0.283$ over the base model). However, the stored knowledge is not recoverable by similarity: given a query with no subgraph, embedding-based and weight-space geometry retrieval both perform at chance, because a semantically neighbouring entity's adapter does not contain the answer - knowledge is stored locally and does not transfer. Weight geometry correlates with subgraph semantics ($\rho = +0.329$) but not with functional retrievability. We quantify the byte and context-token costs against graph retrieval-augmented generation and discuss deployment implications. Our results establish that parametric knowledge graph memory is feasible for storing knowledge, and identify selecting and composing the right adapters by a mechanism other than semantic similarity as the central open problem - motivating a learned, query-conditioned composition mechanism.

    中文

    图检索增强生成会在查询时将检索到的子图放入模型上下文窗口，因此每次查询都要付出重复的 token 成本，并暴露源数据。我们研究一种替代方案：将知识图谱离线编译成一组 LoRA 适配器，每个实体对应一个适配器，作为参数化知识层；查询时通过注入权重而非文本来访问，从而无需占用查询时的上下文。在 MetaQA 数据集上，我们发现，通过子图训练的适配器编码了与上下文无关、能够泛化到未见问题的事实知识：对于单值关系，适配器的精确匹配分数比几乎无法进行闭卷回答的基础模型高出 $+0.243$，$0.007$；只有正确的适配器才能找回这些知识（其相对于基础模型的 oracle 差距为 $+0.283$）。然而，无法通过相似性找回所存储的知识：在没有子图的查询中，基于嵌入和权重空间几何的方法检索效果都处于随机水平，因为语义上相邻实体的适配器并不包含答案——知识是局部存储的，不会迁移。权重几何与子图语义相关（$\rho = +0.329$），但与功能性可检索性无关。我们量化了相较于图检索增强生成的字节和上下文 token 成本，并讨论部署影响。我们的结果证明，参数化知识图谱记忆可用于存储知识，并指出核心开放问题在于如何通过语义相似度之外的机制选择并组合正确的适配器——这促使人们探索经过学习、由查询条件化的组合机制。

    Wenbo Wang, Di Sang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper isolates how mismatches between model emissions and serving interfaces censor tool-use trajectories, and shows that adapter and parser changes restore tool execution without a detected held-out success gain. This gives substantial empirical insight into agent-system observability and evaluation; model behavior is incidental to the interface mechanism, with no clear contribution to interpretability, composition, or reasoning.

    本文阐明了模型输出与服务接口不匹配如何删失工具使用轨迹，并展示了修改适配器和解析器能够恢复工具执行，但未检测到留出任务成功率提升。这为智能体系统的可观测性和评估提供了重要的实证见解；模型行为只是接口机制中的次要因素，对可解释性、组合性或推理没有明显贡献。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Tool-use evaluations typically measure calls through a serving stack, which can report zero calls even when model outputs contain call-shaped payloads. We study interface-induced trajectory censoring: a mismatch between model emissions and the interface that converts them into actions. On selected BFCL v4 subsets, changing only the serving adapter while holding model weights and other evaluation settings fixed moves scores under the official scorer from 0.00 to 0.96 on simple_python and from 0.00 to 0.19 on multi_turn_base. A template-parser factorial experiment shows strong complementarity: neither component replacement alone restores parsing from the baseline, whereas their joint replacement recovers 196/200 first-request parses. Across five Qwen2.5-Coder checkpoints, classifier-positive emissions increase with model size while the mismatched interface reports no calls; a separate matched-interface Qwen3 ladder exhibits few silent emissions through 8B. Experiments on 115 tau-bench retail tasks extend the mechanism to a stateful, non-code environment. In a preregistered, single-seed, 150-step 7B LoRA experiment, changing only the parser registered in verl increases tool executions from 10 to 16,844. However, neither a shared programmatic-feedback evaluation nor a post-hoc common native function-calling evaluation detects a held-out success gain from repair; rescue counts do not increase. Interface repair thus restores tool-mediated experience without a detected performance gain in this setting. These findings show that tool-use measurements depend on the model-interface configuration and motivate layer-wise observability and conformance checks before attributing evaluation or training outcomes to the model alone.

    中文

    工具使用评估通常通过服务栈测量调用；即使模型输出中含有类似调用的负载，服务栈也可能报告调用次数为零。我们研究接口诱发的轨迹删失，即模型输出与将其转换为行动的接口之间不匹配的现象。在选定的 BFCL v4 子集上，在模型权重和其他评估设置不变的情况下，仅更换服务适配器，就使官方评分器上的 simple_python 得分从 0.00 升至 0.96，multi_turn_base 得分从 0.00 升至 0.19。模板与解析器的析因实验显示二者具有很强的互补性：单独替换任一组件都无法恢复基线解析能力，而同时替换两者则恢复了 200 次首请求解析中的 196 次。在五个 Qwen2.5-Coder 检查点上，分类器判定为阳性的输出会随模型规模增大而增加，与此同时，不匹配的接口仍报告没有调用；另一个接口匹配的 Qwen3 系列模型实验表明，在 8B 及以下规模中，静默输出很少。在 115 个 tau-bench 零售任务上的实验，将这一机制扩展到了有状态的非代码环境。在一项预注册、单随机种子、150 步的 7B LoRA 实验中，仅更换 verl 中注册的解析器，就使工具执行次数从 10 次增加到 16,844 次。然而，无论使用共享的程序化反馈评估，还是事后统一的原生函数调用评估，都未检测到修复带来的留出成功率提升；获救案例数也没有增加。因此，在这一设置下，接口修复恢复了由工具介导的经验，但未检测到性能提升。这些发现表明，工具使用测量取决于模型与接口的配置，并提示在将评估或训练结果归因于模型本身之前，应进行分层可观测性和符合性检查。

    Yihao Ai, Beibei Lin, Weilong Yan, Huaijian Zhang

    Recommendation Reason 推荐理由

    The paper introduces a trajectory-level learnability signal to improve offline on-policy distillation from imperfect teachers, with evidence across mathematical reasoning and code generation. Its contribution substantially advances training for reasoning tasks, but does not directly study reasoning mechanisms, compositional generalization, or model internals.

    本文提出轨迹级可学习性信号，以改进从不完美教师进行的离线同策略蒸馏，并在数学推理和代码生成任务上提供了证据。其贡献显著推动了推理任务的训练方法，但并未直接研究推理机制、组合泛化或模型内部机制。

    阅读摘要 Abstract

    ENGLISH

    Offline on-policy distillation gains efficiency by collecting student trajectories and teacher supervision once and reusing them throughout optimization. The same reuse makes imperfect supervision persistent. Since even strong teachers can fail, we ask \emph{what remains learnable from imperfect teacher supervision?} Teacher failure is only a coarse problem-level signal and does not imply that all supervision along the associated student trajectory is unhelpful. A natural alternative is to estimate teacher recoverability along the trajectory, but repeated continuations largely erase the efficiency advantage of offline distillation. We instead use teacher-successful problems to define a cheap reference for what the student can learn. We train on teacher-successful problems and measure how the likelihood of each observed token in trajectories from teacher-failed problems changes. We use these signed likelihood changes as an operational \emph{learnability signal}: larger increases indicate behavior more strongly promoted by successful-only learning. We aggregate this signal into trajectory-level weights for the original distillation loss. Unlike continuation-based estimates, our learnability requires no additional generation and can be computed once from stored trajectories and model checkpoints. Across mathematical reasoning and code generation, our method improves an offline OPD baseline by up to 2.7 percentage points and matches or outperforms online OPD variants on multiple benchmarks. Despite the additional successful-only distillation stage, it uses 2 GPUs and about 22 GPU hours, compared with 3 GPUs and 36--48 GPU hours for representative online OPD methods.

    中文

    离线同策略蒸馏通过一次性收集学生轨迹和教师监督信号，并在整个优化过程中重复使用，来提高效率。同样的重复使用也会使不完美的监督信号持续存在。既然强大的教师也会失败，我们要问：\emph{从不完美的教师监督中还能学到什么？} 教师失败只是粗粒度的问题级信号，并不意味着相关学生轨迹上的所有监督都没有帮助。一种自然的替代方案是估计教师沿轨迹进行恢复的能力，但反复续写会大幅抵消离线蒸馏的效率优势。我们改用教师成功解决的问题，作为学生可学习内容的低成本参照。我们在教师成功解决的问题上训练，并测量教师未能解决的问题所对应轨迹中，每个已观察 token 的似然如何变化。我们将这些带符号的似然变化用作操作性的\emph{可学习性信号}：增幅越大，说明仅使用成功样本进行学习越能强化相应行为。我们将该信号聚合为轨迹级权重，用于原有的蒸馏损失。与基于续写的估计不同，我们的可学习性方法无需额外生成，只需利用存储的轨迹和模型检查点计算一次。在数学推理和代码生成任务中，我们的方法使离线 OPD 基线最高提升 2.7 个百分点，并在多个基准上达到或超过在线 OPD 变体。尽管增加了仅用成功样本进行蒸馏的阶段，该方法仅使用 2 块 GPU 和约 22 个 GPU 小时；相比之下，有代表性的在线 OPD 方法需要 3 块 GPU 和 36–48 个 GPU 小时。
